title: Add a bias to every row
starter:
%x  = buffer 12 dtype=f32 slot=0
%b  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 12 dtype=f32 slot=2
# x is 3x4, b has 4 values. Store y[i][j] = x[i][j] + b[j].
%v  = load %x
%m  = reshape %v shape=[3 4]
%b0w = shrink %b 0 shape=[]
%b0 = load %b0w
%be = expand %b0 shape=[3 4]
%r  = add %m %be
%f  = reshape %r shape=[12]
%s  = store %y %f
%y1 = after %y %s

hints: The starter adds `b[0]` to everything. Each column needs its own bias.
`expand` only grows size-1 axes. Give b a size-1 row axis first: shape `(1, 4)`.
`reshape %bv shape=[1 4]`, then `expand ... shape=[3 4]`, then `add` it to the 3x4 x.

answer.code:
%x  = buffer 12 dtype=f32 slot=0
%b  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=1
%y  = buffer 12 dtype=f32 slot=2
%v  = load %x
%m  = reshape %v shape=[3 4]
%bv = load %b
%br = reshape %bv shape=[1 4]
%be = expand %br shape=[3 4]
%r  = add %m %be
%f  = reshape %r shape=[12]
%s  = store %y %f
%y1 = after %y %s
answer.explain: `expand` copies along size-1 axes only, so the bias vector is first reshaped to one row, `(1, 4)`, and then expanded to `(3, 4)`: element `[i][j]` reads `b[0][j]`. That's broadcasting made explicit. The `1e8 + 1` test checks the add rounds to f32 like any other.
